title: Brain-inspired spiking neural network frameworks for multimodal spatiotemporal brain data integration: a case study on EEG-fMRI data
title_zh: 脑启发式多模态时空脑数据整合框架：基于EEG-fMRI数据的案例研究
abstract: Abstract Multimodal data integration advances brain informatics by capturing complementary spatial and temporal characteristics of neural activity, leading to more accurate and biologically meaningful representations of brain function. The well-established brain measurement modalities, including electroencephalography (EEG) and functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI), represent fundamental heterogeneity in their temporal and spatial feature representations, making their integration significantly challenging. This study proposes biologically inspired Spiking Neural Network (SNN) frameworks for multimodal spatiotemporal brain data integration using early, intermediate, and late fusion strategies, including a novel ensemble-based explainable X-Meta late-fusion classifier. Methodologically, it extends SNN reservoir architectures to support multimodal learning across separate reservoirs for EEG and fMRI, enabling the modelling of cross-modal interactions. The fusion frameworks were evaluated on a resting-state simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset for decoding the Eyes-Closed (EC) and Eyes-Open-Eyes-Closed (EOEC) brain states and benchmarked against conventional machine learning (using alpha alone and multiple bands) and deep learning approaches. We investigated two EEG representations: raw amplitude and Power Spectral Density (PSD), each integrated with fMRI, to evaluate how the EEG feature representation influences multimodal fusion performance. Our results show that all fusion strategies significantly outperformed unimodal fMRI, with accuracy improvements exceeding 6.6–18%. Improvement over the EEG modality was representation-dependent: for PSD-EEG, post-reservoir fusion strategies improved accuracy by 2.1–4.21%, whereas for raw-EEG, improvements were smaller, with intermediate fusion and X-Meta providing approximately 1.3% gains, reflecting differences in the relative discriminative strength of the modality under each representation. In addition to classification, X-Meta provided model-level feature attribution, identifying EEG and fMRI features associated with previously reported functional brain regions while also highlighting potential exploratory candidate markers. Overall, the proposed frameworks advance brain-inspired computational modelling by not only improving brain-state decoding but also providing interpretable insights into the features contributing to the model’s decision.
abstract_zh: 摘要 多模态数据整合通过捕捉神经活动的互补空间和时间特征，推动了脑信息学的发展，从而获得更准确、更具生物学意义的脑功能表现形式。已建立的脑成像模态，包括脑电图（EEG）和功能性磁共振成像（fMRI），在时间和空间特征表示上存在显著异质性，使得其整合面临显著挑战。本研究提出了基于生物启发的脉冲神经网络（SNN）框架，用于利用早期、中间和晚期融合策略整合多模态时空脑数据，其中包括一种新型基于集成的可解释X-Meta晚期融合分类器。从方法角度来看，该研究扩展了SNN储备架构，以支持跨独立储备的多模态学习，专门用于EEG和fMRI，从而实现跨模态交互的建模。所提出的融合框架在休眠状态同时EEG-fMRI数据集上进行了评估，用于解码眼睛闭合（EC）和眼睛开闭-眼睛闭合（EOEC）脑状态，并与传统机器学习（仅使用α波和多个频带）和深度学习方法进行了基准测试。我们研究了两种EEG表示形式：原始幅度和功率谱密度（PSD），每种形式均与fMRI整合，以评估EEG特征表示如何影响多模态融合性能。我们的结果表明，所有融合策略均显著优于单模态fMRI，准确率提升超过6.6–18%。相较于EEG模态，改进幅度取决于表示形式：对于PSD-EEG，后储备融合策略使准确率提升2.1–4.21%，而对于原始-EEG，改进幅度较小，中间融合和X-Meta提供了约1.3%的提升，这反映了在每种表示形式下模态相对区分度的差异。除了分类任务外，X-Meta还提供了模型级特征归因，识别出与先前报道的脑功能区域相关的EEG和fMRI特征，同时也突出了潜在的探索性候选标记物。总体而言，所提出的框架通过不仅改善脑状态解码而且提供模型决策中贡献特征的可解释性见解，推动了脑启发式计算建模的发展。
